test: the welcome page names Kothari's and says what TableTurn is
what_should_happen: When the app opens on the welcome page, a small line names the restaurant and where it is. The big heading reads "Twenty-two tables." with "No wipe-clean board." on its second line, and the paragraph under it starts with the words about an honest wait.
exact_words: Every party gets a place in the queue and an honest wait

test: on a fresh evening the counts read 22 tables, 22 free right now and 0 in use
what_should_happen: On a fresh evening nobody has been seated. Once the welcome page has read the floor, its three counts read 22 tables, 22 free right now and 0 in use.

test: with one table seated and another waiting to be cleared, free right now shows 20 and in use shows 2
what_should_happen: Before the page opens, one party sits at a table and another party has left its table, which nobody has wiped yet. The counts come from the real floor, so 20 tables are free right now and 2 are in use, out of 22.

test: the drawing shows the table tops T01 to T04, T11 to T13 and T19, and no other table
what_should_happen: The small drawing beside the heading shows exactly eight table tops from the real floor. They are T01 to T04, T11 to T13 and T19, and no other table number appears on the page.

test: the drawing is only a picture: clicking a table top does nothing
what_should_happen: Clicking a table top in the drawing does nothing. The address stays on the welcome page and no panel opens.

reason: Whether each table top in the drawing looks free, seated or to be cleared is a colour and a drawing, and the drawing is hidden from screen readers.

test: before the floor is read the counts show 0 and the drawing is empty, then both fill in
what_should_happen: In the first moment, before the floor has been read, the counts show 0 and the drawing has no table tops. A moment later both fill in by themselves, with no reload: 22 tables, 22 free right now, and the table tops appear.

test: under "Who are you today?" there is one card each for Meera, Joseph, a guest and Ravi
what_should_happen: Under "Who are you today?" a line says that each person sees their own screens and changes the same floor. There are four cards, Meera the host, Joseph on the floor, a guest and Ravi the manager, each with its one-line description and "Continue as" with the person.
exact_words: Each person sees their own screens. Everything they do changes the same floor.
Runs the host stand. Sees every table, keeps the waitlist and seats each party.
Works the floor. Marks a table when the party leaves, and again once it is wiped.
Gives a name at the stand. Sees the wait they were quoted and, once seated, the wait they had.
Owns the restaurant. Reads every party’s record.

test: "Continue as Meera" opens Meera's floor at /host/floor
what_should_happen: Clicking Meera's card opens her floor. The address becomes /host/floor.

test: "Continue as Joseph" opens Joseph's tables at /staff
what_should_happen: Clicking Joseph's card opens his tables. The address becomes /staff.

test: "Continue as a guest" opens the guest's wait at /guest
what_should_happen: Clicking the guest's card opens the guest's own wait. The address becomes /guest.

test: "Continue as Ravi" opens Ravi's board at /manager/board
what_should_happen: Clicking Ravi's card opens his board. The address becomes /manager/board.

test: Tab reaches the four person cards in order, and Enter opens the one in focus
what_should_happen: Pressing Tab through the page reaches Meera's card, then Joseph's, the guest's and Ravi's, in that order. Pressing Enter on the card in focus opens that person's screen.

reason: Where the drawing sits and how many cards stand in a row at phone width is layout, which a pretend browser does not draw.

test: every page has the TableTurn mark with "Kothari's · Baner", and clicking it opens the welcome page
what_should_happen: At the top of Joseph's screen sits the TableTurn mark with the name "TableTurn" and "Kothari's · Baner". Clicking it opens the welcome page at /, which has the same mark.

test: on the welcome page the header has no back arrow and no person button
what_should_happen: On the welcome page nobody has been picked yet. The header shows the TableTurn mark, but no back arrow and no person button.

test: on /staff the back arrow comes before the TableTurn name, and the person button shows J, Joseph and Floor staff
what_should_happen: On Joseph's tables the first thing Tab reaches is the back arrow, named "Back to the home page", and the next is the TableTurn name. On the right a person button shows his initial J, "Joseph" and "Floor staff".

reason: That the person button sits on the right of the header is layout, which a pretend browser does not draw.

test: the back arrow on a person's screen opens the welcome page
what_should_happen: On Meera's floor, clicking the back arrow opens the welcome page at /. The back arrow is then gone, because nobody has been picked.

test: the person button opens "View the restaurant as" with the four people and their roles
what_should_happen: Clicking the person button opens a menu that starts with "View the restaurant as". It lists four people with their roles, in order: Meera the host, Joseph on the floor, a guest and Ravi the manager.

test: in the person menu the person whose screens these are is marked as the current one
what_should_happen: Joseph opens the person menu on his own screen. His option is marked as the current one, so a screen reader says so as well as the tick showing it. Meera, the guest and Ravi are not marked.

reason: The tick beside the current person is a drawing, and the menu opening under the button is layout, so only a real browser shows them; that the current person is marked for a screen reader is tested above.

test: choosing Ravi closes the menu and opens his board at /manager/board
what_should_happen: With the person menu open, clicking Ravi closes the menu. Ravi's board opens at /manager/board and the person button now names Ravi.

test: a click outside the person menu closes it and nothing else changes
what_should_happen: With the person menu open, a click anywhere outside it closes the menu. The page stays on Joseph's tables and the button still names Joseph.

test: Esc closes the person menu and nothing else changes
what_should_happen: With the person menu open, pressing Esc closes the menu. The page stays on Joseph's tables and the button still names Joseph.

test: pointing at the guest option opens "Be the guest of" with tonight's parties, newest first
what_should_happen: Kulkarni (6 covers) and then Shah (2 covers) have joined the list. Pointing at the guest option in the person menu opens "Be the guest of" beside it, listing each party with its number, name and covers, newest first: W002 Shah 2, then W001 Kulkarni 6.

test: clicking the guest option opens "Be the guest of" with tonight's parties
what_should_happen: On a computer a click on the guest option first points at it, then clicks it. The list "Be the guest of" must open and stay open with both parties of the evening.

test: Enter on the guest option opens the parties, as a click does
what_should_happen: With the person menu open, Tab reaches the guest option. Pressing Enter on it opens "Be the guest of" with both parties of the evening.

reason: That the list opens beside the menu on a computer, and under the guest option on a phone, is layout.

test: with nobody on the list the guest's list says "Nobody is on the list yet. Add a party as Meera, the host."
what_should_happen: Nobody has joined the list yet. Opening the guest's list in the person menu shows no parties and says "Nobody is on the list yet. Add a party as Meera, the host."
exact_words: Nobody is on the list yet. Add a party as Meera, the host.

test: choosing W001 Kulkarni closes the menu, opens My wait at /guest and names the Kulkarni party in the header
what_should_happen: In the guest's list, clicking W001 Kulkarni closes the menu and opens My wait at /guest. The person button now reads "Kulkarni party" and "Guest · W001", and the guest option in the menu reads the same.

test: on Meera's floor the tabs "The floor" and "Waitlist" sit beside the title, The floor is current, and Waitlist opens
what_should_happen: On Meera's floor there are two tabs, "The floor" and "Waitlist", and The floor is marked as the page she is on. Clicking Waitlist opens /host/waitlist, and Waitlist becomes the current tab.

test: on the Waitlist page the tab "The floor" opens the floor
what_should_happen: On Meera's Waitlist page the other tab is "The floor". Clicking it opens /host/floor.

reason: The current tab being filled in Meera's colour is a colour; the test checks only that it is marked as the current page.

test: with three parties waiting the Waitlist tab carries a badge with 3
what_should_happen: Three parties are waiting on the list. On Meera's floor the Waitlist tab carries a badge that reads 3.

test: with nobody waiting the Waitlist tab has no badge
what_should_happen: The only party of the evening has already been seated, so nobody is waiting. The Waitlist tab reads just "Waitlist", with no badge, not even a 0.

test: the Waitlist badge changes as parties join or are seated, with no reload
what_should_happen: Two parties are waiting, so the badge reads 2. A third joins somewhere else and, within 20 seconds and with no reload, the badge reads 3. Once two of them are seated it reads 1.

test: /host leads to /host/floor
what_should_happen: Opening the short address /host lands on Meera's floor. The address becomes /host/floor and the header names Meera.

test: /manager leads to /manager/board
what_should_happen: Opening the short address /manager lands on Ravi's board. The address becomes /manager/board and the header names Ravi.

test: an address the app does not have, such as /kitchen, opens the welcome page at /
what_should_happen: Opening /kitchen, an address the app does not have, lands on the welcome page. The address becomes / and there is no back arrow.

reason: The page's own scroll bar needs a page taller than the window, scrolling and dragging; a pretend browser has no heights, so the bar never shows there.
